title: dedicated-autoscaler-throughput-burst-controls-util-reporting
author: Daniel Kim
description: Motivation: Customers on Dedicated fleets have reported bursty traffic patterns that cause short-term queueing and missed throughput guarantees. This PR implements a combined token-bucket burst control and throughput smoothing policy in the Dedicated autoscaler and adds utilization reporting hooks so SREs and customers can see burst usage and guarantee violations over time. Summary of changes: 1) Autoscaler: introduce token-bucket based burst tokens per-fleet with configurable refill rates and max-burst capacity; integrate with existing scale-up/down decision pipeline to allow short duration oversubscription when tokens available; add smoothing window to avoid oscillatory scaling on bursty workloads. 2) Throttling/Queuing: add soft-throttle path when tokens exhausted that prioritizes latency-SLO traffic and backpressures best-effort routes. 3) Metrics & Reporting: emit new timeseries (fleet.burst.tokens_remaining, fleet.burst.refill_rate, fleet.burst.allowed_oversubscribe_seconds, fleet.utilization.p95_queue_delay) and tag by customer_id and pool_id; add a utilization report generator that aggregates token usage and guarantee breaches into a daily summary. 4) Config/API: expose new autoscaler config fields (burst: {enabled, refill_per_sec, max_tokens, smoothing_window_sec, priority_threshold}) via the private control-plane API and default to conservative values for existing fleets. 5) Tests & CI: unit tests for token bucket logic, integration test for scale decision pipeline under synthetic burst load, and end-to-end smoke test validating metric emission. Migration notes: config fields are backwards compatible; if not specified, burst controls are disabled and autoscaler behaves as before. Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleets, observe metrics for 72h, then 50% then full. Validation: ran load tests in perf-canary with 1k client rps bursts and verified 95th latency stayed within SLO for prioritized routes while throughput transiently increased up to 1.8x when tokens available. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed ENG-9812 - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Metrics emitted and dashboards updated - [x] Docs and API changes annotated - [x] Feature gated behind config flag - [x] Canary rollout plan documented
commits: Add token-bucket burst controller and unit tests
Integrate burst controller into autoscaler decision loop
Add soft-throttle path and priority handling
Expose config fields in control-plane API and validate schema
Emit burst and utilization metrics and add report generator
Add integration and e2e smoke tests
review_comments: Aisha Gomez: Left a few nits on config naming and suggested making refill_per_min an alias for ease of ops. Please also add telemetry for token consumption rate. Author response: updated config schema and added token_consumption_rate metric.

Priya Nair: Concerned about interaction with existing cluster-autoscaler overrides; requested an integration test that simulates cluster autoscaler preemption. Author response: added integration test in services/autoscaler/integration/scale_decision_test.go that triggers a simulated preemption path and validated fallback.

Liam O'Connor: Approved after addressing two comments around log verbosity and adding a feature flag. Author: rebased and squashed commits, reduced log level for high-frequency paths, added feature gate (burst.enabled) and documented safe defaults.
release_notes: Introduce token-bucket burst controls and utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets. This enables short-term oversubscription to improve latency for priority traffic while providing visibility into burst consumption and guarantee breaches. Feature is off by default and can be enabled via autoscaler.burst config.
